ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, in triangle $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, the angle bisector of $\angle CAB$, $AD$, intersects $BC$ at $D$, $DE\perp AB$ at $E$, $DE=2\,\text{cm}$, and $DB=4\,\text{cm}$. What is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because$AD bisects $\angle$CAB, and DE$\perp$AB at E, with $\angle$C=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$CD=DE=2,\\
Also $\because$ $DB=4\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$BC=BD+CD=4+2=\boxed{6}\text{(cm)};

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper left, and a right-angle mark is marked at C; D is located on side BC, and AD is connected; E is located on the base AB, and the line segment DE from D to E is drawn. The problem text gives that AD is the angle bisector of ∠CAB, DE⊥AB, DE=2 cm, DB=4 cm. Reasoning: Because D is on the angle bisector AD of ∠CAB, the perpendicular distances from D to the two sides AC and AB of the angle are equal. The perpendicular distance from D to AB is DE; and because ∠C=90°, AC⊥BC, and D is on BC, DC⊥AC, therefore the perpendicular distance from D to AC is DC. Thus DC=DE=2 cm. D is on BC, and DB=4 cm, so BC=BD+DC=4+2=6 cm.
